summary: Reviewed in 10 chunks. A hardcoded production backend URL is introduced in the frontend proxy config, breaking all local dev environments and creating a critical production-only deployment. | Router inconsistencies and a behavioral change in action execution can cause runtime errors. | The diff refactors 7 services to use exceptions instead of ApiResponse wrappers, which is correct per project conventions, but introduces a critical AttributeError in Permission.__init__ due to __slots__ + setattr conflict, and has a behavioral regression in the Permission singleton pattern. | All changes in this chunk correctly migrate services to raise exceptions instead of returning error responses, and update tests accordingly — no regressions or bugs introduced. | Tests in this chunk correctly update call sites to match a service-layer refactor that removes session injection, converts async methods to sync, and changes return types from ApiResponse wrappers to direct values — consistent with a framework migration. | This chunk contains safe, cleanup-only changes: removing unused imports, replacing quoted string type annotations with proper TYPE_CHECKING imports, removing two genuinely unused variables (c1_resp, c1_id), and multi-line reformatting of long strings. No critical bugs, regressions, or security issues introduced. | All changes correctly migrate tests from the old ApiResponse/status-enum pattern to the new direct-return/exception pattern, with no regressions introduced. | A single incorrect assertion in test_ticket_service.py uses dict-style access on a ticket object returned by the refactored API, which would cause the test to incorrectly pass or behave unpredictably.

critical_issues.description: Production backend URL 'https://agent-job-production.up.railway.app/api/:path*' is hardcoded as the rewrite destination, replacing the local localhost:8000 dev server. This breaks local development for all frontend engineers — every dev environment will proxy to production instead of the local backend. This is an architectural regression that must be reverted or made environment-dependent (e.g. via NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL env var).

Endpoint `create_user` uses `session=Depends(get_db)` without the `AsyncSession` type annotation, inconsistent with `tickets.py` and most other endpoints in this same file. This makes type checking unreliable and diverges from project conventions (CLAUDE.md rule: type session as `AsyncSession` with no default).
Endpoint `list_users` uses `session=Depends(get_db)` without the `AsyncSession` type annotation. Same issue as above.
Endpoint `get_user` uses `session=Depends(get_db)` without the `AsyncSession` type annotation. Same issue as above.
Endpoint `update_user` uses `session=Depends(get_db)` without the `AsyncSession` type annotation. Same issue as above.
Endpoint `delete_user` uses `session=Depends(get_db)` without the `AsyncSession` type annotation. Same issue as above.
Endpoint `search_users` uses `session=Depends(get_db)` without the `AsyncSession` type annotation. Same issue as above.
Endpoint `change_password` uses `session=Depends(get_db)` without the `AsyncSession` type annotation. Same issue as above.
Endpoint `register` uses `session=Depends(get_db)` without the `AsyncSession` type annotation. Same issue as above.

`create_user` returns `result.data` when `UserService.create_user` returns an `ApiResponse` with `status=SUCCESS`. If `data` is `None` (e.g., the created user returned `None` as data), the method returns `None` instead of a dict. All callers (e.g., `users.py` `register`) do `return {"success": True, "data": result, ...}` — passing `None` as `data` produces a malformed response. Also, when `result.status != SUCCESS`, the method raises `ValidationException`, but the unwrapping logic does not handle the case where the service returns a plain dict (non-`ApiResponse`) — it would fall through and return a raw dict that may lack expected fields.

In `_execute_action`, the old code checked `result.status.value == "success"` to determine action success vs failure and embed that in the returned dict. The new code replaces this with `if result:` — a behavioral change that changes what gets returned regardless of the actual result's success state. Additionally, if `NotificationService.send_notification` returns an ORM object (as the new service pattern intends), it will always be truthy, making the status always "sent" even on failure. Same issue at line 96 for `task_result`.

Permission.__init__ calls setattr(type(self), attr, self) to auto-register an instance as a class attribute, but the class defines __slots__ = ("value",). In Python, __slots__ controls only instance attributes — class attributes (stored in type(self).__dict__) are unaffected. However, this new auto-registration design is a regression vs. the old _mk() singleton pattern: the old code stored instances in a _registry_ dict and returned the same object on repeated calls, while the new code overwrites the class attribute each time, making Permission objects non-singleton. Code relying on Permission.CUSTOMER_CREATE is_permission.CUSTOMER_READ identity checks (e.g. caching in tests) will break, even though __eq__ still works by value. Additionally, if any code ever accesses Permission._registry_, it will get KeyError since that dict no longer exists.

Assertion `assert result["assigned_to"] == original_agent` uses dict-key access on a MockTicket object. After the refactoring, `auto_assign` returns a `MockTicket` with `.assigned_to = 3`, but `original_agent` (from `sample_ticket.assigned_to`) is `None` (since `TICKET_ROW` has no assigned_to key and MockTicket.__init__ defaults it to None). With MagicMock's permissive __getitem__, `result["assigned_to"]` returns a MagicMock rather than the actual value, making the comparison unreliable. The assertion should be `assert result.assigned_to == original_agent` (dot-notation attribute access), consistent with every other test in the file that was updated in this refactor.

suggestions.description: All router endpoints have removed response_model=... OpenAPI annotations. Clients relying on OpenAPI schema generation or FastAPI's automatic docs will lose typed response definitions. Consider restoring response_model or using a simple Pydantic envelope schema so API consumers retain type information.

max-turns was increased from 20 to 100 — a 5x increase. Confirm this is intentional; a 100-turn LLM review could consume significant compute budget per pipeline run on all PRs across all branches, not just develop.

Trigger changed from 'schedule + push to develop' to 'pull_request + push on all branches [*]'. This means every push to every branch (including feature branches) will run the full pipeline. Verify this is intended, as it significantly increases CI compute usage.

list_automation_rules now returns _paginated(items, total, page, page_size) but items may be ORM objects that need .to_dict() conversion — the _paginated helper calls i.to_dict() on each item, but the old response_model guarantees are gone.
All session parameters should be annotated as `session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)` for consistency with tickets.py and to satisfy the project's service convention.

Consider returning `result` directly (after unwrapping) instead of `result.data`, and ensure callers handle the unwrapped dict shape consistently. Also guard against `data` being `None`: `return result.data if result.data is not None else {}`.

Restore the status-check logic: inspect the actual return value of `NotificationService.send_notification` and `TaskService.create_task` to determine success/failure, rather than relying on truthiness alone.
The module docstring references `Ticket/TicketReply` objects having `.to_dict()`, but `TicketReply` is not directly used in the router (only `Ticket` via service). Consider clarifying the docstring.

`remove_widget` returns `False` instead of raising `NotFoundException` like the other methods (`get_dashboard`, `update_dashboard`, `add_widget`, `run_report`). For consistency with the new exception-raising pattern, consider raising `NotFoundException` here too.
`delete_dashboard` returns a list but has no return type annotation. Given the in-memory store pattern, consider adding a type annotation and ensuring the return value is meaningful to callers.

create_customer can return None when the INSERT returns no row (e.g. constraint violation). The router must handle None and convert it to a proper error response, since the service no longer raises an exception in this case. Verify all callers handle the None case, otherwise a None.to_dict() or similar TypeError will occur at the router layer.

update_customer returns None when set_clauses is empty. The router should handle a None return from this method — either by converting it to a 200 with an empty data payload or treating it as a no-op response, to avoid downstream TypeErrors.

The __slots__ = ("value",) declaration is correct (prevents arbitrary instance __dict__), but the class-level setattr design means Permission instances are not singletons. If backward compatibility with code doing Permission.CUSTOMER_CREATE is_permission.CUSTOMER_READ identity checks is needed, restore the _registry_ dict and return cached instances. If identity doesn't matter (only __eq__ by value), add a comment documenting that Permission instances are value objects and not singletons.

set_role_permissions and set_user_roles use list(dict.fromkeys(role_ids)) for deduplication — this is a clever trick but opaque. Consider using a comment like '# deduplicate, preserve order' or factoring it into a small helper to make the intent explicit.

delete_stage returns int (the stage_id). The delete_pipeline method (line 160) also returns int. This is consistent but differs from other methods that return ORM models. Verify all router callers know to expect an int here rather than a dict, since the API contract for deletion now returns a bare ID.

`auto_assign` still returns a raw dict `{"ticket_id": ..., "assigned_to": ...}` instead of a domain model — inconsistent with every other method in the class now returning ORM/model objects or raising exceptions.

`get_user_by_username` is the only method in this file that still returns `dict | None` (implicitly via no raise) instead of raising `NotFoundException` like `get_user_by_id` does — inconsistent with the service pattern being established in this refactor.

The `export_to_csv` case that used to assert `status == "error"` now uses `pytest.raises(ValidationException)` — this is correct, but note that the underlying service method still returns a plain dict `{status: "error", message: ...}` rather than raising on empty data (only `export_to_csv` raises), so the test change is good.

`_mock_session` is a class-level fixture using `autouse=True` that stores a `MagicMock` on `self._session` — this works for the test methods here, but it's an unconventional pytest pattern that may be surprising to future readers.

Module-level state (`_tickets_db`, `_ticket_replies_db`, `_ticket_agent_index`) is used for in-memory persistence across service instances — this is test infrastructure that bypasses the DB session entirely. It works, but it's an important architectural note: the service does not use `self._session` at all for any CRUD operations in this file.

sla_svc.get_breach_tickets() is called with no arguments while the old signature accepted tenant_id. Verify the service extracts tenant context internally (e.g. from a middleware or dependency) rather than via parameter, otherwise this will query across all tenants.

sla_svc.check_sla_status(fetched) is called without await. Confirm check_sla_status is genuinely synchronous in the refactored SLA service — if it is still async, this returns a coroutine and the status assertion will fail at runtime.
svc.get_unread_count(...) is called without await. Confirm the refactored NotificationService made this method synchronous, otherwise this is a missing await that will cause test failures.
File lacks a trailing newline. Ruff may warn about this. Add a blank line at the end of the file.

Variable c2_resp is assigned but its .json() call is invoked twice in succession (lines ~949 and ~955). Consider storing `c2_id = c2_resp.json()['data']['id']` to avoid redundant JSON parsing, consistent with how c1_resp was used before being dropped.

The added `mock_db_session` fixture is not used anywhere in the visible diff — `service` (line ~137) likely still references it from conftest. If it was intentionally scoped here, ensure `service` at line ~137 uses this local fixture; otherwise the unused import and fixture can be removed to keep the file lean.

The section comment `# make_mock_session — key SQL routing behaviours` differs from the base comment `# _make_mock_session — key SQL routing behaviours`. Since `_make_mock_session` was renamed to `make_mock_session`, the comment update is correct but was missed — it will be caught by the next lint pass anyway.
